articles.title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
articles.titleEn: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
articles.abstract: Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the Brassica AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid Brassica napus (AACC) and diploid Brassica rapa (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between B. napus and Brassica oleracea (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with B. rapa . Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both B. napus subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in Brassica diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.

articles.title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction
articles.titleEn: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction
articles.abstract: Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope ( 15 N– 18 O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y −1 . This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.

articles.title: Cognitive diversity and majority rule
articles.titleEn: Cognitive diversity and majority rule
articles.abstract: Societies rely on groups–boards, panels, committees, and representative bodies–to make important decisions for good reason: overwhelming evidence shows groups usually make more accurate choices than individuals. The predominant logic for group accuracy rests on reasoning formulated in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, which states that if voters receive independent and equally accurate generated signals, majority rule produces decisions that i) are more accurate than the average voter, ii) improve in individual accuracy and iii) group size, and iv) approach perfect accuracy as group size becomes large. An alternative logic based on interpreted signals explains the accuracy of majority rule as arising from the aggregation of diverse mental models. Group accuracy results from the same state of the world being classified differently by different people. In this framework, the set of possible group accuracies can be characterized conditional on average individual accuracy and average pairwise diversity. Majority rule groups are only guaranteed to outperform their members when diversity is high. Using data from a variety of empirical settings, along with simulations of a minimal nearest-neighbor model, we find much stronger support for the predictions of the interpreted signals framework than for the standard generated signals model. We further show empirical evidence for a diversity–accuracy paradox, in which more diverse groups are less accurate unless average individual accuracy is nearly constant across groups. Our findings have important implications for group composition and institutional and organizational design as well as for the potential gains from deliberation.

articles.title: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France
articles.titleEn: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France
articles.abstract: Patient movement within and between hospitals creates a complex hospital network that facilitates the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and contributes to healthcare-associated infections. Yet most national-scale studies infer spread from aggregated hospital-to-hospital patient sharing, leaving patient-to-patient contact pathways and the role of routine patient mobility in shaping colonization risk poorly characterized. Using France’s 2023–2024 national hospital-discharge data, we reconstructed a temporal patient-based network of 10.4 million patients across 1,408 acute-care hospitals, comprising 326.6 million overnight ward colocation interactions. We simulated colonization over 365 d on the observed day-by-day temporal network using a stochastic susceptible–colonized–susceptible model, with a mean colonization duration of 180 d. We used national carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) surveillance data to calibrate differences in transmission risk across clinical settings. Across 2,000 simulations initiated on randomly selected dates in 2023, we calculated patient-level colonization probabilities and summarized risk across patients’ residential areas, wards, and hospitals. We further assessed hospital-level consistency between simulated risk and recorded CPE occurrence. Simulated risk was highly heterogeneous across patients and care settings. When mapped by place of residence, hospital-associated colonization risk showed strong spatial clustering in both urban and rural areas. Multivariable regression analyses identified patient- and hospital-level characteristics associated with heterogeneity in simulated colonization risk. Sensitivity analyses varying initial seeding and colonization duration showed that relative risk patterns remained highly stable. This nationwide framework shows how patient mobility and ward colocation patterns can reveal patterns of hospital-associated colonization risk and could support pathogen-specific surveillance and intervention evaluation.

articles.title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
articles.titleEn: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
articles.abstract: High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH) 2 with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li + diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH) 2 to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO 2 . In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li 2 CO 3 disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.

articles.title: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists
articles.titleEn: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists
articles.abstract: Marine protists are key players in marine ecosystems, yet a large fraction, particularly among the smallest taxa, belongs to uncultured lineages lacking genomic data, limiting our understanding of their ecology and evolution. Beyond determining their gene repertoires, genomic information is essential to reveal how genomes are organized. Features such as genome size, GC content, and structural gene architecture represent physical constraints that shape evolutionary fitness and adaptability in marine environments. Here, we present a genomic catalog of 147 marine picoplanktonic protist species, greatly expanding the genomic representation of uncultured and ecologically relevant lineages through a single-cell approach. This dataset enables refined phylogenomic placement of previously uncharacterized marine eukaryotes, including abundant marine protistan players as well as a few species belonging to novel or poorly known groups that are crucial for resolving deep questions in eukaryotic evolution. We uncover pronounced genome streamlining in ecologically successful lineages, coupled with extensive, mostly lineage-specific functional adaptations. At a broader scale, we identify functional traits enriched independently across several marine eukaryotic lineages, including genes involved in complex carbohydrate degradation in heterotrophic organisms and the presence of polyketide synthases. Together, these results provide a framework for investigating the genomic drivers and molecular mechanisms behind the ecological success of marine eukaryotic microbes.

articles.title: A herbivore-induced plant volatile facilitates group foraging in locusts
articles.titleEn: A herbivore-induced plant volatile facilitates group foraging in locusts
articles.abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense strategies against herbivory, often releasing volatile compounds upon attack to deter further feeding. Here, we demonstrate the induced volatile S-linalool promotes phase- and stage-specific group foraging in the migratory locust ( Locusta migratoria ). We show that S-linalool, a volatile whose emission increases more than 10-fold following damage by gregarious nymphs, acts as a potent attractant that drives other nymphs to aggregate and feed on previously attacked rice plants. Mechanistically, we identified the olfactory receptor LmOR49 that detects S-linalool and used genome editing to make this receptor nonfunctional, thereby abolishing both electrophysiological responses and behavioral attraction. We also inactivated rice genes required for S-linalool biosynthesis, abolishing its emission, rendering plants unattractive, and disrupting locust feeding preference. Although feeding on previously attacked plants provides no detectable direct fitness benefit under our experimental conditions, prior locust feeding suppresses the accumulation of deterrent metabolites, potentially increasing plant palatability for subsequent feeding. S-linalool thus serves as an olfactory cue that guides gregarious nymphs toward previously attacked, more palatable plants. Collectively, these findings uncover a comprehensive mechanism whereby a plant defense volatile is exploited by an insect herbivore to promote group foraging, broadening our understanding of plant–insect interactions and suggesting molecular targets for locust control.

articles.title: Quantifying (de)mixing of disordered proteins in molecular dynamics simulations
articles.titleEn: Quantifying (de)mixing of disordered proteins in molecular dynamics simulations
articles.abstract: Biomolecular condensates control the spatial and temporal organization of cellular biochemistry. Their architectures often arise from complex, multicomponent mixtures governed by weak, multivalent interactions between intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of proteins. However, current approaches lack generalizable metrics to determine whether IDRs will mix or segregate within condensates. Here, we present a domain decomposition method (DDM) that accurately determines phase concentrations without identifying condensate interfaces. When tested against 399 IDR simulations, the DDM recovers dense- and dilute-phase concentrations within 1% agreement of established surface-based methods. By calculating spatial variances to map three-dimensional organization, this approach successfully distinguishes homogeneous mixing from surface enrichment, core–shell architectures, and complete segregation. Applying this continuous metric to 2,068 binary mixtures of 32 distinct IDRs, we demonstrate that physicochemical similarity strongly promotes mixing. Hydrophobic IDRs mixed promiscuously across all partner chemistries, whereas charged sequences mixed in a way highly sensitive to charge complementarity, forming the most stable condensates as net charge approached zero. Compared with experimental networks, our IDR-only simulations predicted the partitioning preferences for 10 of 13 proteins, with discrepancies accurately isolating cases where colocalization strictly requires RNA or folded domains. Quantifying mixing in this way provides a robust and reproducible method for predicting IDR interactomes and understanding the composition of complex cellular condensates.

articles.title: An alternative patterning mechanism for vertebrate tooth complexity
articles.titleEn: An alternative patterning mechanism for vertebrate tooth complexity
articles.abstract: How development reliably generates complex patterns remains a central question in biology. Teeth provide an ideal system for addressing this problem, linking cusp-patterning mechanisms to diversification and the fossil record, yet the developmental basis of multicuspid crown patterning beyond mammals remains unresolved. In mammals, cusp initiation and spacing are controlled by transient epithelial signaling centers called enamel knots (EKs). Here, we combine comparative developmental analyses, 3D morphometrics, mutant perturbation, and Bayesian inverse modeling (BITES; Bayesian Inference for Tooth Emergence Simulation) to examine tooth morphogenesis across six squamate species representing convergent multicuspid dentitions. We find that cusp patterning in these taxa does not rely on a discrete EK-based patterning system. Instead, cusps arise from a broad, persistent cusp signaling field (CSF) that deploys canonical tooth-patterning pathways but lacks the spatial restriction, apoptosis, and discrete secondary EKs (SEKs) characteristic of the mammalian system. Changes in epithelial growth and signaling are associated with disproportionate expansion of this field during tooth development and with the formation of additional cusps. Quantitative variation in field extent and dynamics can generate crown morphologies within and across species, providing a developmental basis for positional heterodonty and repeated gains and losses of multicuspidity in squamates. Our results identify an alternative epithelial patterning architecture for vertebrate cusp formation, in which conserved tooth-patterning signals are deployed through a broad field-based architecture rather than compact signaling centers. Together, these findings revise how tooth developmental complexity is encoded and show how similar complex crown forms can evolve through distinct flexible epithelial patterning mechanisms.

articles.title: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis
articles.titleEn: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis
articles.abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine–leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

articles.title: When Heavy Tails Disrupt Hydrologic Modeling
articles.titleEn: When Heavy Tails Disrupt Hydrologic Modeling
articles.abstract: Heavy tails (HT) appear in a myriad of hydrologic applications, and their presence can disrupt common hydrological, statistical and machine learning methods. Most prior hydrologic literature on HT distributions focused on their impact on the estimation of floods and droughts, whereas we discuss their impact on the performance of hydrologic modeling methods. Examples of HT distributions reviewed here include rainfall‐runoff model residuals, river discharge, water quality loads, daily residential water use, atmospheric surface layer flows, and saturated hydraulic conductivity of soils. We review known impacts of HT populations on the instability and bias associated with the commonly used bootstrap method as well as a wide class of common hydrologic statistics, including the Nash–Sutcliffe and Kling–Gupta efficiencies, coefficients of variation, skewness and kurtosis, correlations, and even the ubiquitous sample mean. Very HT distributions can induce severe instability associated with a wide class of hydrologic modeling methods commonly reported in the literature with some of the most severe impacts associated with the calibration, validation, and application of deterministic rainfall‐runoff models. Product moments (i.e., variance, skew, etc.) can be infinite for some HT populations, yet analogous upper L‐moments always exist, thus the theory of L‐moments is uniquely suited to HT applications. The theory of L‐moments also provides a practical tail heaviness index, L‐kurtosis, which can alert us to HT conditions when disruption to hydrological modeling and inference can be expected. Practical responses to heavy tail behavior include transformations, robust statistical methods, representation of tail behavior, and, where appropriate, temporal aggregation.

articles.title: LESSONS report: Fine-scale representation of consecutive dry days
articles.titleEn: LESSONS report: Fine-scale representation of consecutive dry days
articles.abstract: The number of consecutive dry days (CDD) is a widely used metric for assessing meteorological drought. This study investigates spatial CDD patterns over Germany during the drought year of 2018, comparing a convection-permitting model (CPM) at 3 km resolution with ERA5 reanalysis at 31 km, gauge-based interpolated observations at 1 km, and radar measurements at 1 km. The analysis reveals a surprise : high-resolution CPM and radar data produce strikingly heterogeneous, “brushstroke-like” spatial structures that differ fundamentally from the smooth fields of reanalysis and gridded observations. Our report confirms that these sharp spatial discontinuities are not computational artifacts but a physical consequence of the sensitivity to the fixed daily dryness threshold of the CDD metric. We find that the CPM can well reproduce these fine-scale patterns that are also detected by radar measurements, which is quantified by a spatial autocorrelogram and the radially averaged power spectral density. While averaging CDD over multiple years smooths out the brushstroke patterns, such temporal averaging does not resolve the underlying shortcoming : multi-year CDD is built upon individual annual CDD values that are, as shown here, highly variable and strongly dataset-dependent. A statistic whose single-year realizations are dominated by threshold-crossing noise provides an unstable foundation for climatological analysis regardless of the aggregation period applied. As a lesson learnt, CDD depends on the spatial resolution of the data and, at the kilometre scale, on single precipitation events close to the threshold; CDD should therefore only be compared between data sets of similar resolution and interpreted with caution at individual grid cells or stations, including in drought monitoring, impact assessment, and climate model evaluation. This study reports on the surprising fine-scale spatial patterns and resulting shortcomings of the CDD metric and is therefore submitted as a LESSONS report, a paper category dedicated to documenting Limitations, Errors, Surprises, Shortcomings, and Opportunities for New Science.
articles.abstractEn: The number of consecutive dry days (CDD) is a widely used metric for assessing meteorological drought. This study investigates spatial CDD patterns over Germany during the drought year of 2018, comparing a convection-permitting model (CPM) at 3 km resolution with ERA5 reanalysis at 31 km, gauge-based interpolated observations at 1 km, and radar measurements at 1 km. The analysis reveals a surprise : high-resolution CPM and radar data produce strikingly heterogeneous, “brushstroke-like” spatial structures that differ fundamentally from the smooth fields of reanalysis and gridded observations. Our report confirms that these sharp spatial discontinuities are not computational artifacts but a physical consequence of the sensitivity to the fixed daily dryness threshold of the CDD metric. We find that the CPM can well reproduce these fine-scale patterns that are also detected by radar measurements, which is quantified by a spatial autocorrelogram and the radially averaged power spectral density. While averaging CDD over multiple years smooths out the brushstroke patterns, such temporal averaging does not resolve the underlying shortcoming : multi-year CDD is built upon individual annual CDD values that are, as shown here, highly variable and strongly dataset-dependent. A statistic whose single-year realizations are dominated by threshold-crossing noise provides an unstable foundation for climatological analysis regardless of the aggregation period applied. articles.title: Multi-year convection-permitting irrigation impacts across the European continent
articles.titleEn: Multi-year convection-permitting irrigation impacts across the European continent
articles.abstract: Irrigation is an important anthropogenic activity that can impact surface and atmospheric conditions. In fact, global, regional and local studies that included irrigation in Earth system models already demonstrated the effects of irrigation in different variables. Some regional and local simulations have studied the irrigation impact in some parts of Europe with simulations limited to the duration of one growing season. However, long-term irrigation simulations that cover the whole European continent are still missing. This study quantifies the long-term impact of irrigation on surface and atmospheric variables over the EURO-CORDEX domain using convection-permitting simulations with the Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) model that cover a period of 12 years. Our findings indicate that the magnitude of the irrigation impact is limited by the irrigated region and the climate conditions of a given year in the EURO-CORDEX domain, showing that the land–atmosphere coupling is key to determine the irrigation effects. For instance, the cold and wet summer of 2017 in south Europe weakened the irrigation cooling in the Alps. In contrast, the heat wave of 2018 in Central Europe enabled the influence of irrigation on surface variables in this region. Regarding precipitation, we found no robust climatological precipitation response to irrigation across the 12 year analysis. Our results highlight the importance of representing irrigation in climate models across Europe, given its region-specific impact and increasing relevance, especially as the frequency of extreme events such as droughts and heat waves is projected to increase.

articles.title: Coupling LaMEM 3.0.1 and FastScape 2.8.4 for self-consistent 3D thermo-mechanical and landscape evolution modeling
articles.titleEn: Coupling LaMEM 3.0.1 and FastScape 2.8.4 for self-consistent 3D thermo-mechanical and landscape evolution modeling
articles.abstract: The feedback between tectonic events and surface processes shapes both landscapes and lithospheric deformation, yet 3D numerical models that couple thermo-mechanical processes with landscape evolution remain uncommon, partly due to mismatches in temporal and spatial scales between the two. Here, we present a coupling module implemented within LaMEM that couples the thermo-mechanical code LaMEM with the landscape evolution code FastScape. The method transfers surface velocities from the parallel LaMEM grid to a persistent FastScape grid, subdivides each thermo-mechanical timestep into landscape evolution substeps, and returns the updated topography to LaMEM for free-surface and material-phase updates. The module supports 2D and 3D LaMEM configurations, as well as both uniform and non-uniform thermo-mechanical grids. Parameter and resolution tests demonstrate stable behaviour across the investigated buoyancy, bedrock erodibility, hillslope diffusivity, and surface grid settings. A comparison between a 2D-coupled and a fully 3D configuration of a plume-induced dome shows that the 3D model captures the dome-shaped uplift and radial drainage. A 3D subduction model with an oceanic plateau demonstrates the module in a large-scale application with along-strike variability. The source code, input files, and a user manual for the presented tests are archived in a persistent public repository.

articles.title: Idealised framework to prescribe sea surface temperatures to investigate the atmospheric circulation response
articles.titleEn: Idealised framework to prescribe sea surface temperatures to investigate the atmospheric circulation response
articles.abstract: Midlatitude sea surface temperature (SST) fronts exert a strong influence on storm tracks and westerly jets by modulating lower-tropospheric baroclinicity, moisture availability, and diabatic heating. Yet the sensitivity of the large-scale atmospheric circulation to the detailed structure of these fronts remains difficult to isolate in realistic model configurations. Here we introduce an idealised SST framework for aquaplanet experiments that allows to prescribe the strength, width, and latitude of a midlatitude SST front. The SST profile is constructed from analytically derived meridional gradients, ensuring that changes to the front generate physically consistent moisture distributions through the Clausius–Clapeyron relation. Using this framework, we conduct a suite of sensitivity experiments to quantify the influence from various aspects in the structure of the SST front on the climatological-mean energy and water cycles as well as the associated atmospheric circulation. Preliminary results demonstrate that increasing the frontal SST gradient or narrowing the frontal width systematically intensifies storm-track activity and strengthens the midlatitude jet, whereas shifting the front meridionally alters the latitudinal position of storm tracks in a non-linear manner. Warm- and cold-climate experiments further show that imposing a fixed freezing threshold in atmosphere-only setups artificially reduces high-latitude baroclinicity, whereas allowing SSTs to go below freezing produces a more realistic polar thermal structure. Overall, our results demonstrate that the experimental framework developed in this study provides a useful basis for targeted process studies of how midlatitude SST-front characteristics shape the atmospheric circulation, energy budget, and hydrological cycle.

articles.title: A new Monte Carlo treatment of multiple scattering of light by black carbon aggregates with varying levels of compactness
articles.titleEn: A new Monte Carlo treatment of multiple scattering of light by black carbon aggregates with varying levels of compactness
articles.abstract: We use a specially designed Monte Carlo (MC) model that includes individual Mueller matrix selection in each scattering event to conduct a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the intensity and polarization of light multiply scattered by an atmospheric layer embedded with black carbon (BC) particles with varying compactness. We find that the spatial distributions of the degree of linear and circular polarization are sensitive to BC particle shape, and that depolarization is more dominant for spherical BC particles than for fractal aggregates. We also find that the layer transmittance is highest for the more spherical BC particle shapes and lowest for the extended fractal aggregates, with an overall difference of approximately 10 % relative to the incident intensity between the highest and lowest values of transmittance. We find that the reflectance exhibits a similar tendency, and that correspondingly, the layer absorptance is lowest for the more spherical BC shapes and highest for the extended fractal aggregates. In addition, we compare the results obtained from our MC simulations with those obtained with the delta-Eddington approximation for the same optical thickness, single scattering albedo, asymmetry factor, and incident zenith angle. We find that there is a relatively small difference between our results and the delta-Eddington results with respect to the layer transmittance and the layer absorbance, but that the layer reflectance obtained with our MC simulations is up to 50 % lower than that obtained with the delta-Eddington approximation. These results could have important implications for radiative forcing estimations, climate modeling, and remote sensing implementations.

articles.title: Drivers of reduced permafrost cooling efficacy of equatorial stratospheric aerosol injection in the Eastern Arctic compared to a moderate emission pathway
articles.titleEn: Drivers of reduced permafrost cooling efficacy of equatorial stratospheric aerosol injection in the Eastern Arctic compared to a moderate emission pathway
articles.abstract: The Arctic is warming about four times faster than the global average, with permafrost thaw representing a potential global climate tipping element. Given the insufficient rate of carbon emission reductions, stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has emerged as a strategy to abate climate warming. However, its effects on permafrost thaw drivers remain uncertain. The G6sulfur and G6solar experiments, part of the Geoengineering Model Intercomparison Project (GeoMIP6), aim to offset the warming in the high-emission scenario (ssp585) to achieve global-mean near-surface air temperatures comparable to those in the moderate-emission scenario (ssp245), through the injection of stratospheric aerosols near the equator (G6sulfur) or a reduction in top-of-atmosphere solar irradiance (G6solar), respectively. Analyzing both experiments, we find that G6sulfur alters atmospheric circulation, modifying winds, cloud properties, and the North Atlantic Oscillation, which affect temperature patterns and longwave radiation. These changes shift the relative importance of mechanisms driving summer permafrost thaw, resulting in a robust east–west dipole in thaw depth (+0.769 m, 6/6 models): increased thaw in the Eastern Hemisphere (+0.491 m) and a significant but less model-consistent reduction in thaw in the Western Hemisphere (−0.278 m), compared to the ssp245 scenario targeted by the intervention. While both G6sulfur and G6solar slow permafrost decline by 2080–2099 relative to ssp585 (+4.61 × 10 6 and +5.37 × 10 6 km 2 respectively), neither preserves as much permafrost area as ssp245 (−1.08 × 10 6 km 2 for G6sulfur and −0.32 × 10 6 km 2 for G6solar). By altering the drivers of permafrost dynamics, G6sulfur creates spatial variations in thaw patterns, resulting in an overall reduction in permafrost area compared to ssp245. Our findings underscore the need to better understand and optimize SAI deployment to avoid unintended regional impacts.

articles.title: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
articles.titleEn: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
articles.abstract: Karst groundwater systems exhibit heterogeneity in recharge, circulation, and discharge, occupying a unique position within groundwater systems. This complexity facilitates rapid responses via the preferential flow routes, making karst systems vulnerable to climatic and anthropogenic pressures. High-altitude karst aquifers are particularly susceptible to shifting climate patterns – specifically rising temperatures, declining snow cover, and increasingly less and inconsistent precipitation – within the Mediterranean climate hotspot. Effective sustainable management of these groundwater systems require robust hydrological modelling; however, the application of such models is often constrained by the availability of high-quality, reliable datasets. This study presents a comprehensive collection of high-resolution karst spring discharge data from major Euro-Mediterranean mountain belts, including the Atlas, Betics, Pyrenees, Jura, Alps, Carpathians, Apennines, Dinarides, Hellenides, Balkans, Taurus, Levant, and Zagros. We compiled a total of 129 discharge time series specifically curated for hydrological modelling. Geographically, the dataset is led by the Alps (approx. 38.7 %), followed by the Carpathians (11.7 %) and Dinarides (approx. 8.5 %), the Apennines, and Zagros each contributing approx. 6.2 %. The Levant, Pyrenees and Taurus account for approx. 5 % each, while the remaining regions (Atlas, Balkans, Betics, Hellenides, and Jura) represent less than 5 % each. In terms of temporal resolution, 92 % of the records are daily, while hourly and monthly data each comprise 4 %. The average record length is 21 years, which is led by a 98-year series from Unica Spring, Slovenia (1926–2024). Regional analysis indicates that the Jura, Balkans and Pyrenees maintain average record length exceeding 30 years of daily data, followed by the Alps, Apennines, Betics, Carpathians, and Dinarides, exceeding 20 years, whereas the Atlas, Levant, Taurus, and Zagros range between 10 and 20 years. The shortest average records were observed in the Hellenides (8 years), which is still adequate for hydrological modelling applications. The dataset can be accessed at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19448790 (Çallı et al., 2026).

articles.title: A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
articles.titleEn: A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
articles.abstract: Agricultural lime has historically been applied to croplands in the United States to counteract soil acidification and enhance soil fertility, with important consequences for crop productivity and Earth's carbon cycle. Previous works on agricultural liming have largely focused on either region-specific case studies or national-level estimates of total application rates, leaving a major gap in understanding the spatial variability in lime application. This study addresses this gap by presenting the first spatially explicit dataset of agricultural lime application across the contiguous United States (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15758274, Tsao et al., 2026). The dataset comprises state-level data for 1930–1950 and a more detailed county-level dataset for 1954–1987, enabling comprehensive spatial-temporal analyses at multiple scales. Counties in the Midwest region exhibited the highest total amounts of lime applied in the latter half of the twentieth century, reflecting intensive agricultural activity. These counties were characterized by higher overall lime application rates (amount of lime applied per unit of limed area each year) but relatively lower lime-treated fraction (ratio of limed area to total cropland area each year). In contrast, counties in the southeastern coastal region exhibited lower lime application rates per unit of limed area but with a higher lime-treated fraction within the agricultural areas. We used a machine learning framework to assess if the spatial variation of lime application from our dataset can be explained by agricultural and environmental factors with known agronomic relationships. Our results show that the total amount of lime applied for each county, as well as the application rate and treated fraction, can be reasonably explained with regional climatic conditions, soil properties, and agricultural management practices (such as crop production, fertilizer use, and soil pH recommendations). Spatiotemporal integration of the data product results in a revised national estimate of total lime application, with a range of 15–25 million metric tons per year (Mt yr −1 ) between 1954–1987. This study establishes a critical observational baseline of historical agricultural lime application and highlights the need for further research into its long-term environmental impacts.

articles.title: The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
articles.titleEn: The consistent in-situ global gridded temperature and salinity dataset, CORA OA 1960–2024
articles.abstract: Gridded ocean products play a pivotal role in oceanographic and climate research, providing a framework for the cross-validation and calibration of satellite observations and in-situ data. This paper describes the latest evolution of the global gridded ocean objective analysis fields for temperature and salinity, distributed by the Copernicus Marine Service. It accounts for the update of the objective analysis first guess using monthly fields derived from the temporal interpolation of World Ocean Atlas 2023 (WOA23) decadal temperature and salinity climatologies. The new product provides monthly objective analysis fields for temperature and salinity with a 0.5° horizontal resolution and 186 vertical levels covering depths from 0 to 5500 m. The dataset is updated annually and covers the period from 1960 to December of the last complete year; the version described here covers 1960–2024. A full reprocessing is conducted every November, while an interim update covering the first six months of the current year is released each June. This product was compared with other reference 3D temperature and salinity datasets, as well as SST and SSS products. It exhibits strong consistency with all reference data, particularly over the 1985–2024 period. Notably, the effects of the Argo “fast salty drift”, detected in other datasets after 2016, are limited in this product. The gridded product is freely available from the Copernicus Marine Service at https://doi.org/10.48670/mds-00383 (E.U. Copernicus Marine Service Information (CMEMS), 2026) (product ID INSITU_GLO_PHY_TS_OA_MY_013_052).

articles.title: Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
articles.titleEn: Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
articles.abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a proposed carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) removal strategy via the application of crushed silicate rocks to accelerate the natural breakdown of silicate minerals, permanently trapping atmospheric CO 2 . Application of rock dust may alter soil properties, such as pH, with potential consequences for soil trace gases fluxes relevant to climate forcing and air quality. However, previous ERW studies have focused mainly on the principal greenhouse gases, while broader trace gas responses remain poorly constrained. This laboratory study presents measurements of nitric oxide (NO), ammonia (NH 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen (H 2 ) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), as well as CO 2 , methane (CH 4 ) and nitrous oxide (N 2 O), from control and ERW-treated soils collected from arable, grassland and newly planted broadleaf and conifer forest field trials in the UK. Soils were sieved, repacked and rewetted for laboratory measurements. A dynamic air-flow-through chamber system, equipped with a high-resolution multi-gas analyser and a proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometer, was used to measure N 2 O, NO, NH 3 , CO, and VOCs between 5 and 25 °C. CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes were measured online at 20 °C using a closed-loop chamber method, and H 2 fluxes were measured by discrete sampling from static chamber headspace using gas chromatography. ERW-associated differences varied among gases and soils, with no consistent response across all incubated samples. The reported treatment differences included lower CO 2 emissions in both forest soils, greater CH 4 uptake in broadleaf forest soil, higher NO emissions in grassland soil, and changes in CO and hydrocarbon fluxes in forest soils. NH 3 and H 2 fluxes showed no statistically significant treatment responses, and no individual VOC remained significantly different after correction for multiple testing. Overall, rock dust application had limited and inconsistent impacts on trace gas fluxes across the soils examined in this study. As these measurements represent snapshots of field ERW effects under controlled laboratory conditions from manipulated soils, longer-term in-situ measurements at ERW field trials are needed to examine how these responses vary seasonally and evolve as the applied materials continued to weather. These measurements should be accompanied by in-depth soil characterisation and microbial analyses to elucidate the complex relationships between ERW treatment and trace gas fluxes. This evidence is needed to assess the full climate, air-quality and environmental implications of large-scale ERW deployment.

Overall, rock dust application had limited and inconsistent impacts on trace gas fluxes across the soils examined in this study. These measurements should be accompanied by in-depth soil characterisation and microbial analyses to elucidate the complex relationships between ERW treatment and trace gas fluxes. This evidence is needed to assess the full climate, air-quality and environmental implications of large-scale ERW deployment.

articles.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
articles.titleEn: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
articles.abstract: Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
articles.titleEn: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
articles.abstract: The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

articles.title: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
articles.titleEn: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
articles.abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8 + T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm ). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti- Lm CD8 + T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8 + T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm . These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

articles.title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
articles.titleEn: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
articles.abstract: Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

articles.title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
articles.titleEn: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
articles.abstract: Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Post‐2100 Climate Change
articles.titleEn: A Systematic Review of Post‐2100 Climate Change
articles.abstract: Climate services seek to inform decisions about long‐term climate changes. Since the 1990s, the vast majority of climate projections have covered the period up to 2100, a horizon that is not so distant anymore. This leaves decision makers tasked with planning coastal development or building long‐lived infrastructure with relatively sparse information to assess climate risks, evaluate the costs and benefits of adaptation options, and implement carbon emission mitigation actions. In a bid to better understand how climate services could extend further into the future, this paper reviews the literature to understand how and why post‐2100 climate studies are conducted. It identifies three broad themes: understanding climate processes with great inertia, assessing climate risks and informing adaptation actions, and evaluating emission mitigation scenarios. Multiple papers reveal the complex interplay between climate feedbacks, and show how climate change post‐2100 is not merely an extension of 21st century trends. The overwhelming focus on the current century downplays the long‐term damages of current emissions and fails to convey the possibility that future climate conditions could exceed adaptation capacity. We reiterate numerous calls made in the literature to extend mainstream climate emission scenarios and climate model projections farther into the future, and provide the building blocks for robust climate products.

articles.title: Who Migrates? Social Identity and the Limits of Climate Adaptation
articles.titleEn: Who Migrates? Social Identity and the Limits of Climate Adaptation
articles.abstract: Migration is increasingly framed as a key climate adaptation strategy, yet this framing often overlooks how social hierarchies structure the feasibility of migration. We investigate this relationship in South India, a critical development context characterized by high caste stratification, out‐migration, and rainfall variability. We conceptualize migration as a threshold process in which household capacity increases the feasibility of moving, while social identity may constrain the translation of capacity into adaptive action. Using repeated cross‐sectional data from 27,122 households linked with high‐resolution rainfall data, we estimate migration responses to rainfall variability across different caste groups. We find that marginalized caste groups have substantially lower migration probabilities under normal rainfall conditions, but they become significantly more responsive as rainfall anomalies become more severe. This pattern suggests a bifurcation in adaptation behavior: while advantaged groups migrate more under typical conditions, marginalized groups are more responsive to severe rainfall stressors. Counterfactual simulations show that migration gaps persist even when household capacities are equalized. These findings suggest that adaptation inequality is not merely a problem of endowment deficits but of identity‐based constraints tied to caste, requiring policies that address the structural barriers to adaptation.

articles.title: Large Projected Increase in Cloud‐to‐Ground Lightning Under Future Climate
articles.titleEn: Large Projected Increase in Cloud‐to‐Ground Lightning Under Future Climate
articles.abstract: Cloud‐to‐ground (CG) lightning poses significant risks to infrastructure, people, and ecosystems. However, while many studies have projected changes in total lightning under warming, future trends in CG lightning remain poorly constrained. Here, we combine ground‐based CG lightning observations with six daily surface meteorological variables (mean temperature, total precipitation, short‐wave radiation, relative humidity, pressure, wind speed) to predict CG lightning density over land at 0.5° resolution using an XGBoost machine learning model. The model accurately captures contemporary spatial and temporal lightning patterns and outperforms an alternative multiple linear regression model as well as three existing parameterizations based on convective precipitation or convective available potential energy times precipitation. Applying the XGBoost model to historical climate shows a 11% increase in global CG lightning frequency over the 20th century. Future projections using outputs from two climate models (MPI‐ESM1‐2‐HR and UKESM1‐0‐LL) reveal large increases of 76%–140% under a high‐emission scenario (SSP3‐7.0), equivalent to roughly 30% more CG lightning per degree of global warming. These increases are substantially higher than those projected by the linear model and previous studies. Absolute increases are largest in the tropics, while relative increases are largest at high latitudes, where lightning density often more than doubles. The largest uncertainties emerge in the tropics for UKESM1‐0‐LL climate, particularly in the Amazon and New Guinea, where future climate differs strongly from current conditions. Our results suggest that climate change may substantially amplify CG lightning frequency, underscoring the need for improved risk assessments.

articles.title: Weather Sensitivity to Sea Surface Temperatures Over the Contiguous United States in a Medium Ensemble of High‐Resolution Regionally Refined Simulations Using E3SM
articles.titleEn: Weather Sensitivity to Sea Surface Temperatures Over the Contiguous United States in a Medium Ensemble of High‐Resolution Regionally Refined Simulations Using E3SM
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Climate model simulations have long been invaluable tools for synoptic meteorology. However, they are generally too coarse in resolution to resolve fine‐scale extreme weather, which require stronger spatial gradients and sharper representations of topography. Here we perform an ensemble of sea surface temperature (SST)‐forced experiments with the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, applying its regionally‐refined model capability over the contiguous United States. The prescribed SSTs are historically‐derived and designed to represent recurrent patterns of Pacific Ocean variability. Our ensemble allows for understanding of how leading modes of ocean variability affect global hydroclimate but with the added capacity to resolve extreme weather at regional scale over the US. We focus our study on how ocean modes of variability specifically affect extreme heat and extreme precipitation events, snowpack, tropical cyclones, and atmospheric rivers. We find that extreme weather is realistically simulated at regional scale but shown to have a persistent wet precipitation bias and warm temperature bias, which impacts the utility of the ensemble. Nonetheless, our simulations provide a large sample of highly impactful extremes, including extremes possible over the historical period but without a historical analog, and their response to ocean variability.

articles.title: Porous Cavities and Smooth Boundaries: Brinkman Volume Penalization for Ice‐Shelf–Ocean Interactions in Ocean General Circulation Models
articles.titleEn: Porous Cavities and Smooth Boundaries: Brinkman Volume Penalization for Ice‐Shelf–Ocean Interactions in Ocean General Circulation Models
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Numerical ocean models remain essential for investigating ice–shelf–ocean interaction to estimate the fate of the Antarctic Ice Sheet in a warming climate. A persistent challenge in ‐coordinate ocean models is the artificial stepwise representation of cavity geometries, which induces excessive diapycnal mixing and numerical noise beneath the ice draft. Here, we assess the potential of the Brinkman Volume Penalization (BVP) method for ice–ocean modeling, in which the ice–ocean interface is replaced by a porous region that is partially ocean and partially ice. The benefits of penalization are evaluated in a ‐coordinate ocean model using an idealized ISOMIP+ configuration (Asay‐Davis et al., 2016, https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd‐9‐2471‐2016 ) under both warm and cold scenarios. First, smoothing the cavity with the BVP acts as an effective local increase in vertical resolution, improving ocean circulation near the grounding line and allowing strong basal melt at the ice‐shelf base. Second, we show that the distribution of heat and meltwater within the penalized region reduces spurious mixing, leading to colder and fresher ice‐shelf waters and a strengthened overturning circulation. Hence, the BVP approach provides a promising alternative to a Losch (2008, https://doi.org/10.1029/2007jc004368 ) melt‐layer formulation, for which similar noise reduction requires prescribing a melt‐layer depth that is too large and leads to excessive mixing. Finally, we show that at least four vertical grid cells are required to resolve grounding‐zone overturning and to obtain strong and consistent basal melt patterns. In summary, these results provide practical guidance for improving the numerical treatment of ice‐shelf cavities in OGCMs.

articles.title: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
articles.titleEn: Last glacial North Pacific oxygenation due to North Atlantic circulation changes
articles.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones, subsurface regions of the ocean severely depleted in dissolved oxygen, today extend over more than 30 million km 2 . Although these areas are expected to expand in the future in response to warming, the magnitude of deoxygenation is poorly constrained. Here we present a quantitative spatio-temporal reconstruction of oxygen minimum zone changes in the subarctic and eastern North Pacific over the last 55 thousand years based on 2,569 individual foraminiferal assemblage measurements from 11 sedimentary cores. We find that the extent of oxygen minimum zones in the eastern North Pacific expanded in response to warming during Dansgaard–Oeschger events during the last glacial period and through the last deglaciation. However, re-oxygenation events and oxygen minimum zone contraction also occurred in the last glacial period when overturning circulation weakened in the North Atlantic during Heinrich events. Our findings, supported by Earth system simulations confirming a strong coupling between millennial-scale changes in North Atlantic circulation and North Pacific oxygen minimum zone extent, imply a complex future response of the oxygen minimum zone extent, with global circulation changes potentially mitigating the direct effects of warming.

articles.title: New insights from fully-integrated surface-subsurface hydrological modeling in high-elevation glaciated environments
articles.titleEn: New insights from fully-integrated surface-subsurface hydrological modeling in high-elevation glaciated environments
articles.abstract: Recent modeling efforts go towards distributed physics-based modeling for improved hydrological process understanding. The sparse hydro-meteorological observations and complex topography in high-elevation mountainous environments have, however, hampered the application of such data-intensive and sophisticated techniques for detailed process exploration. In particular, characterizing surface-subsurface water exchange processes in these terrains remains understudied. Here we implement a fully-integrated and fully-distributed surface-subsurface hydrological model, WaSiM , to quantify the observed daily streamflow variations and their interactions with groundwater in the high-elevation glaciated catchment (Martell Valley) in the central European Alps since the 2000s. Extensive field observations (meteorology, vegetation, glacier mass balance, soil properties, river discharge), especially in-situ groundwater levels, were collected to investigate hydrological processes and constrain model parameters in the surface and subsurface. We observe that in contrast to the delayed responses typically observed in aquifers, shallow alpine groundwater responds nearly as quickly as streamflow to peak snowmelt and extreme rainfall events, highlighting the need for improved subsurface parametrization in hydrological modeling. Joint evaluation against shallow groundwater heads and streamflow shows that the daily streamflow and shallow groundwater dynamics can be reproduced without requiring the WaSiM interflow component, providing new constraints on the representation of unsaturated-zone flow pathways in high Alpine hydrological models. Moreover, to improve the integration of point-scale groundwater observations into fully-distributed models, we suggest pre-calculating the Topographic Wetness Index to stratify hydro-topographic settings and combining this information with other site characteristics to guide piezometer placement. Despite uncertainties associated with model structure and subsurface representation, this study demonstrates the value of groundwater observations for constraining internal flow partitioning in hydrological modeling.

articles.title: Enhancing data-driven weather forecasting via gated relative position encoding and spatial-aware feed-forward network
articles.titleEn: Enhancing data-driven weather forecasting via gated relative position encoding and spatial-aware feed-forward network
articles.abstract: Transformer-based weather forecasting models often use static positional encodings, limiting their representation of flow-dependency and geographical heterogeneity. We introduce Gated Relative Position Encoding (GRPE) to address these limitations. Gating mechanism has recently been applied in data-driven weather forecasting, but its specific contribution remains insufficiently understood. We propose Spatial-Aware Feed-Forward Network (SAFN) to explore this question. GRPE constructs dynamic positional biases through a gated linear combination of learnable prototypes, allowing spatial relationships to vary with location and atmospheric state. SAFN combines depth-wise convolutions, multiplicative gating, and a learnable global positional bias to represent spatial feature interactions and persistent geographical influences. We integrate both components into the Neighborhood Attention Transformer for Atmospheric prediction (AtmoNAT), a global forecasting model with 43.4 million parameters trained on ERA5 reanalysis at 1.5° spatial resolution and 12 h temporal intervals. Evaluations using WeatherBench 2 metrics show that AtmoNAT's deterministic forecasts outperform the ensemble-mean forecasts of several other coarse-resolution models across most key variables at lead times up to 72 h. Over global land areas, AtmoNAT also outperforms several models trained at 0.25° resolution, including FuXi and GraphCast, for 10 m winds and 700 hPa specific humidity at lead times up to 120 h. Ablation experiments show that GRPE and SAFN each reduce root mean square errors by approximately 5 %–10 % across most evaluated variables, while individually increasing parameter counts and computational costs by only approximately 1 %–4 %. These results demonstrate that adaptive positional encoding and spatially aware feature gating can improve weather forecasting accuracy with modest computational overhead, highlighting the profound potential of GRPE and SAFN in advancing next-generation weather forecasting.

articles.title: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
articles.titleEn: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
articles.abstract: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions and management poorly constrained. Here, we utilize simulations from the latest Land-Use Model Intercomparison Project to disentangle and quantify the responses of NSWS to different types of LULCC over China from 1970 to 2014. We demonstrate that the primary-to-grazing transition is the dominant factor contributing to LULCC-induced NSWS variability, followed by fertilizer use, while urbanization makes the smallest contribution among the examined LULCC types. Future projections further suggest that land-use pathways can substantially perturb wind patterns, with low-emission pathways combined with minimally regulated land use producing more pronounced alterations than high-emission pathways combined with sustainable land use. These results highlight the importance of resolving LULCC in attributing and projecting NSWS changes, with implications for climate modeling, wind-energy assessment, and land-use policy.

articles.title: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
articles.titleEn: Historical Nansen cast temperature profiles and the ocean heat content changes since 19th century
articles.abstract: Ocean heat content (OHC) estimates rely on subsurface temperature observations whose abundance, quality, and accuracy have changed over time as oceanographic techniques and methods have developed. The majority of the available global OHC time series begins in the 1950s when the International Geophysical Year 1957-1958 (IGY) observational campaign resulted in a rapid improvement of the observational basis. However, a significant amount of subsurface temperature observations had already been accumulated before the IGY. Extending knowledge back in time beyond current estimates provides further insight into global changes in the ocean-atmosphere system. We perform a three-step quality control (QC) of the Nansen cast temperature profiles with a focus on the time period before 1970. The QC includes automated and manual control of temperature observations, along with the quality control of temperature anomalies. We use the World Ocean Circulation Experiment/Argo Global Hydrographic climatology, based on high-quality temperature observations between 1990 and 2025, as the reference. To interpolate temperatures vertically, we use the temperature anomaly method by Frankignoul (1981). This method yields smaller interpolation errors than linear interpolation and the Reiniger and Ross (1968) parabolic method. Corrections for depth bias in Nansen cast profiles are also suggested. The oldest temperature profiles from the 1870s are treated separately, with the data from the “Challenger” expedition used as reference. Finally, we estimate the OHC changes between the 1870s and the 2020s for six selected multi-year time periods. We find that for the layer 0–2000 m the OHC increase between 1920–1944 and 1945–1969 amounts to 32.7±6.8/37.5±3.8 % of the total OHC increase between 1920–1944 and 2010–2025 for original and depth corrected profiles respectively. The complete dataset is freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22764102 (Gouretski et al., 2026a) and https://doi.org/10.12157/IOCAS.20260520.001 (Gouretski et al., 2026b).

articles.title: Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
articles.titleEn: Dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey along the embankment of the Po river in Crescentino
articles.abstract: For river embankment characterization non-invasive geophysical investigations are a valuable complementary tool to standard geotechnical testing. To this aim, resistivity and seismic methods can be complementary to each other, providing information about pore fluid properties and solid skeleton characteristics, respectively. The use of streamer cables for these surveys can reduce the acquisition time, making geophysical investigations ideal as a preliminary screening tool for the identification of localized anomalies. Few examples of combined seismic and electric streamer systems were already proposed in the literature, but their applicability for long and extensive surveys still needs to be showcased. Moreover, tailored processing methods are necessary given the large amount of data collected with the above mentioned acquisition systems, which can be challenging for standard processing and inversion software and require calibration of devoted interpretation techniques. We present a dataset of a 4 km combined seismic and electric streamer survey acquired along the embankment of the Po River in Crescentino, near Torino, in north-west Italy. Data acquisition strategies are discussed and preliminary data analyses are reported. The survey demonstrated the efficiency and potentiality of combined seismic and electric streamer systems in investigating river embankments. All the acquired geophysical data, together with complementary geotechnical, topographic and meteorological information, are made available in a structured dataset (Vergnano et al., 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18183049). The presented dataset can be an ideal playground to test and benchmark alternative processing and interpretation approaches, and enable an advancement in the state-of-the-art of these characterization methodologies.

articles.title: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
articles.titleEn: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
articles.abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a key variable for characterizing marine phytoplankton biomass and upper-ocean biogeochemical variability. Existing global products are generally limited to the ocean surface and therefore cannot adequately resolve subsurface vertical structure. In this study, a multimodal Profile-Surface Transformer (PST) framework was developed by integrating Biogeochemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) Chl a profiles, Core-Argo temperature-salinity profiles, and satellite-derived surface Chl a to reconstruct the three-dimensional (3D) vertical structure of Chl a from 10 to 500 m depth. A global monthly mean 3D Chl a dataset at 1° spatial resolution for January 2005–June 2025 was subsequently constructed. Evaluation of the dataset demonstrates that PST exhibits robust stability and effective profile reconstruction capability across various generalization scenarios. The coefficients of determination under random split, year-based split, and spatial cross-validation are 0.89, 0.87, and 0.86 ± 0.01, respectively. Furthermore, independent external validation using ship-based observations confirms that the model maintains good generalization performance across different observing systems. The constructed dataset successfully reproduces known global patterns of Chl a vertical structure and its subsurface chlorophyll maximum (SCM), as well as their seasonal variability. Variability in SCM depth is primarily characterized by regionally heterogeneous redistribution superimposed on a persistent zonal background, rather than by a pronounced monotonic change in the global mean depth. Overall, the constructed long-term 3D Chl a dataset integrates surface observations and discrete biogeochemical profiles, delivering a new observationally constrained global product. This dataset is well-suited for studies on the vertical ecological structure of phytoplankton, long-term ocean biogeochemical variability, and the responses of upper-ocean ecosystems to climate change. The dataset is publicly available from Zenodo (Meng et al., 2026a) at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22726410.

articles.title: Towards a global database on building architecture and construction materials for urban climate models
articles.titleEn: Towards a global database on building architecture and construction materials for urban climate models
articles.abstract: Due to regional climate change exacerbated by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, the population of dense urban areas is vulnerable to heat stress. Accurate urban climate models are essential for quantifying UHI mitigation strategies and supporting climate adaptation efforts. These models require input data on urban form, materials, and function. However, existing frameworks, such as Local Climate Zones (LCZ) and Geoclimate, only provide urban morphological parameters and lack detailed information on building materials and Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems. To address these limitations, architects, engineers, urban climatologists and researchers in many countries have been contacted via a survey platform to provide information on building materials and HVAC systems. The survey has been translated into 11 languages to enable global coverage. This approach captures significant architectural and construction trends by collecting key data on building envelope characteristics (e.g., walls, roofs, windows, and insulation) and HVAC systems. The survey yielded 521 responses from 141 countries, demonstrating substantial global coverage. A multi-step imputation strategy was applied to create a comprehensive global database, and residential building typologies are defined for each country. Global homogeneous typologies are defined for non-residential buildings. The resulting datasets are freely available (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16096963, de Carvalho Araujo et al., 2025) and can easily be combined with LCZ maps. These datasets provide a valuable resource for urban climate modeling and facilitate more accurate urban climate assessments on a global scale. Future work may enhance data granularity further, for instance, by providing typologies at the subnational level.
